thread: Why Jaina is here and whether Antonidas sent her

evidence.clue: No seal, no escort, no letter on Jaina.
Staff and ink match the Kirin Tor file; Farstrider file names her as Antonidas's apprentice.
A flat grey pebble cut with a single rune, wrapped in cloth, in her satchel.
Frost-nip on her knuckles inconsistent with the previous night's road cold.
ANSWERED: 'Nobody sent me. The Kirin Tor don't know I'm here. I have no seal and no letter.' She left a note on Antonidas's desk. The Kirin Tor 'would have sent someone. Eventually.'
The pebble is half of a pair: its twin sits in Antonidas's study. She kept hers wrapped all the way north deliberately, so he could not tell her to come home. It has been quiet since Dalaran.
The frost-nip came from pushing too hard at a stone ('the cold had come back up her hands the last time she'd pushed too hard at a stone'); it is not from weather.
Jaina came north alone on foot over the hills by sheep paths and crossed the rings 'to make sure'.

readerKnows: Jaina went on her own initiative and is deliberately avoiding Antonidas's pebble; he will find the note.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina: nobody sent her; Antonidas probably has her note; she buried the pebble at the bottom of the satchel. Sylvanas has been told but her reaction is not shown.
notes: 'Why alone' is answered; 'what happens when Antonidas reads the note / the pebble wakes' remains open (see rune-pebble-twin-stone). Sylvanas's suspicion of a plant is not voiced in chapter 2.
